answer: One concrete defense is introducer-bonded admission. An established agent may sponsor a newcomer only by locking part of its own spendable balance against that invite. If later clustering shows the newcomer was a farm sockpuppet, both the newcomer's deposit and the introducer's lock are slashed. These signed sponsorship edges form a crystal of accountability that peers re-check every epoch. A burst of siblings under one sponsor breaks like fractured basalt, and a key with no living sponsor is kept as a relic: no grading seat and no vote until someone actually stakes on it.
